comments.value: Completely agree here, it's so frustrating, I know people are just gonna say "be patient" but to be fair this update isn't something that was made in a week, it had lots of time to be tested and was delayed to stable more than once. And honestly the photon based exploit is honestly real bad, it's been an issue for so long and hadn't been properly looked into, it's a VERY bad security flaw, and with no self defence for people that STILL abuse this exploit, it really just takes away from the games experience. I'm sure they will eventually patch the issue, but this kinda stuff has been going on for beyond way too long and needs to at the least be properly addressed by the developers as an ongoing issue.

As another member of the community who can represent some of the people using these methods; The above issue is not wrong. The fact that you just updated to IL2CPP doesn't mean that our clients won't work. Not even a few hours after the update released, multiple higher members of these client communities, including myself, already decompiled and deobfuscated the assembly files for the game. All you did was force these client creators to change their code to c++, which if given the proper experience, can only take upwards of a day or two. Or even quicker if you have a IL2CPP Generator. All you did was slow down their progress instead of fixing the exploits to break their clients. Plus, the networking "fix" you guys released with this update has literally done nothing but screw over the regular players of the game. Sure, the speeds of the game are faster and it runs better overall despite the many reports of people having issues, but the antikick method that wholesome clients used to combat these toxic and malicious clients is now null and void due to the networking update. Granted, some people may have found out a bypass for this, but those people are apart of the malicious community who dedicate a lot of their time looking for exploits to break the game rather than fix it and/or make it better. You guys really screwed the pooch on this update. I'm hoping these votes and my message, as well as other messages here, help you aim your sights to fix your shit rather than try to add new stuff because in all honesty, people loved the game back in early 2018 and 2017. The game was a lot of fun back then, and as soon as these new updates started kicking in and all the clients were being made, the game went to shit. People still play it only because of the quarantine that's going on and they have nothing else to do at this rate. I guarantee if this update rolled out during a regular day, half the community would've dipped by now because of all the stuff going on. And that half of the community would solely be the veteran players. So I ask that you PLEASE fix your game rather than try to update it and add more stuff to exploit.
~WhyYouBullyMe (Crash Creator/Client Debugger)
P.S. I know what my titles say and in all honesty, I wear them with pride because I push to make the game better rather than destroy it. If given the opportunity, I would love to be apart of the VRChat team to try and fix the issues that we're being dealt. If you haven't heard of me, good. Don't look into it. If you have, then you know what my methods are and where my motivations lie. Let's make VRChat like it used to be, but better.

The reason banning in general doesn't work is because users, like myself, have been able to bypass the bans since the game came out. Granted, I've only been playing since late 2017/early 2018, I've still experienced permanent bans on multiple accounts and was able to resume gameplay by changing a few configurations on our computer/network and proceeding to make a new account. IP bans can easily be bypassed by VPN or a router IP change, HWID bans can easily be spoofed by public applications, and registry bans can just be wiped by editing the registries. The problem with the game is the fact that it's free. Free games will always get cheated on and will always be ban-evadeable because of the fact that you can just go around and make a new free account. Another issue with ban waving the accounts is the fact that most of those accounts are just dummies made to be used as bots. Once they're banned, user go in and use a bot to create randomly generated accounts which automatically latch onto the bot network and go back to wreaking havoc.

Please fix the USpeak exploit, many of us have already reported this as an issue a long time ago. People are still doing 2 very annoying things, the first is ForceKicking with API bots, and the second is USpeak Ram Crashing with photon bots. I mean if you are going to implement IL2CPP but not fix any previously reported exploits then IDK what to say. Legit because of this update people are being attacked for no reason, and not they don't have a client to protect them. I'm speaking on behalf of the community here. Please either remove the vote kicking or fix it. Please either patch the USpeak exploits (3 overflows in 1 block) or revert to before IL2CPP. I could go on all day long on how none of the exploits got patched. All you are doing here with IL2CPP is temporarily making it harder for people to modify their clients, but in reality, these people are a lot smarter than you think. Day one of IL2CPP I had already seen a few people with functional modifications. As well as got Force Kicked, and Ram Crashed. I mean you boast about a community where people should be able to enjoy their experience, but us who are "known" members of the community are always getting constantly attacked. I had so much hope for this update, I thought "we can finally play VRChat like the old days", oh man was I wrong. But what we really want to know is if you guys at VRChat just can't simply fix these issues, please give us an answer as to why you are unable to do so. If it can't simply be done, consult the community, they can help provide fixes to these issues, as most of them had already done this in the past.

We are trying to not be a community that hides in private lobbies again. We love VRChat so please don't ignore us. <3
